item.title: Slow Turnout At Kaduna Polling Unit As INEC Holds Mock Accreditation
item.description: There is a slow turnout at polling units 031 and 032 in Ungwan Boro, Sabon Tasha ward, in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State, as there is little to suggest that the mock accreditation exercise set to hold today by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is taking place. As at the time of filing this report, at exactly 9:29 am , officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission were yet to be on ground to commence the exercise scheduled to commence by 8:3am. The only security presence observed is that of three personnel of the Nigeria Security CIVIL Defence Corps (NSCDC) There is also no presence of voters at the two polling units, raising questions about the level of preparedness and awareness ahead of the exercise. The situation contrasts with INEC’s earlier assurance of readiness for the mock election, which is designed to assess its operational capacity and the effectiveness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and result transmission technology ahead of the 2027 general elections. As at Friday night, when voting materials were distributed at the INEC office in Kaduna, the Administrative Secretary, Abba Yahaya, also assured the public of the Commission’s readiness for the mock election, expressing confidence in its preparedness to conduct the exercise. The exercise is expected to simulate the 2027 Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The post Slow Turnout At Kaduna Polling Unit As INEC Holds Mock Accreditation appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Lawal pledges more projects as APC Campaign visits Shinkafi
item.description: Governor seeks support for Tinubu, APC candidates ahead of 2027 polls Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has pledged to execute more development projects in Shinkafi Local Government Area as he canvassed support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. Lawal made the pledge on Friday during the APC Zamfara North campaign flag-off rally held at the Eid ground in Shinkafi. The rally attracted party chieftains, including the Director-General of the Tinubu/Shettima Presidential Campaign Council and former governor, Abdul’aziz Yari; another former governor, Mahmuda Aliyu Shinkafi; the state APC Chairman, Kabiru Moyi; and other party leaders. Tens of thousands of supporters reportedly welcomed the campaign entourage at the town’s entrance, chanting slogans in support of the party. Addressing the gathering, Lawal thanked the people of Shinkafi for their solidarity and warm reception, saying their support was encouraging. He said his administration had recorded achievements in education, healthcare, infrastructure and economic development. The governor disclosed that his administration had rehabilitated six primary healthcare centres, including facilities in Badarawa, Birnin Yero, Galadi, Jangeru and Kurya. He described the ongoing referral hospital project in Shinkafi as a legacy initiative that would transform healthcare delivery in Zamfara State and the North-West. According to him, the project is central to his administration’s commitment to improving access to quality healthcare. Lawal also said his administration had completed 22 of the 31 projects undertaken over the past three and a half years, while the remaining nine were at more than 80 per cent completion. He urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu, his administration and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. “I am here once again to seek your votes. Vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, vote for me, and vote for the APC from top to bottom in the upcoming 2027 general election,” he said. The governor’s spokesman, Sulaiman Bala Idris, disclosed this in a statement issued on November 27, 2026. item.title: Chelsea in a ‘difficult moment’ admits Alonso
item.description: Xabi Alonso admitted Chelsea are in a “difficult moment” as the beleaguered boss urged his struggling side to stick together after their dismal 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest on Friday. Alonso’s side crashed to a third successive Premier League loss to leave them languishing in eighth place. The Blues have lost four of their last five league matches, piling pressure on Alonso just months into his reign at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea fell behind to Igor Jesus’s early opener before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled Forest’s lead with a second half penalty. Emmanuel Emegha reduced the deficit but Gibbs-White struck again to make Emega’s late second nothing more than a footnote on another dispiriting evening for Alonso. “It’s a difficult moment for everyone. It’s disappointing again to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions, we can’t stop,” Alonso said. “We are low in confidence, the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting to 2-1 we have conceded and go to 3-1. “Everything is not going our way, we are responsible for that and we are responsible to find solutions.” Chelsea have already conceded 23 goals in 12 league matches and their porous defence was not helped by Alonso’s curious decision to use Ecuador midfielder Moises Caicedo in a back-three. Alonso also selected Wesley Fofana after the centre-back was forced to apologise for joking in a YouTube interview about missing a penalty during Chelsea’s League Cup defeat against Liverpool this season. The hapless Fofana was booed by angry Chelsea fans at the City Ground and conceded a penalty with his careless foul on former Blues striker Liam Delap. “We need to support everyone. Everyone that is in the team we need to support,” Alonso said of Fofana. “We know we have to go through difficult moments. We don’t take apart anyone and we want to help.” Asked to assess Chelsea’s dismal run, Alonso suggested the only cure was hard work on the training ground. “We can do better for sure. At this level you need to hold results and that is why we are losing in the last games,” he said after Chelsea’s sixth league defeat his term. “That is the only way I understand football. When things are not going well, try to work and find solutions. It can happen that we turn it around and it goes our way.” Chelsea’s sixth league defeat under Alonso will spark pointed questions about the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. Although Alonso led Leverkusen to an historic Bundesliga title in 2024, he lasted just seven months before being sacked by Real. The former Liverpool midfielder desperately needs a win against bottom of the table Crystal Palace on Wednesday to avoid the sack talk growing even louder. “Everyone needs to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it,” he said. The post Chelsea in a ‘difficult moment’ admits Alonso appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ten live bets, zero accumulators: the story of a bettor from Burkina Faso
item.description: No bets on impulse. No chasing miracles. An AfroPari player from Burkina Faso has made a net profit of over 14 millions $ from ten bets, all placed live. Her idea? While everyone else waits for goals, she bets there won’t be many. One match, one slip Her biggest win: over 6,800 $ on a match in Switzerland Plenty of bettors stuff their slips with five, six, even ten events, dreaming of a huge payout, but not her: one event, sensible odds. Betting on silence She watches the game, feels the tempo, and only then makes her move. She’s after tight, cagey matches where nobody wants to take risks. Most of her bets are on goals staying under a certain line, sometimes in the first half only. Best example? Hoffenheim vs Schalke 04. She backed this one twice: first the first half, then the full match. Two bets, two hits. Not just Europe, not just football Big names aren’t her thing. Europe’s top leagues, yes, but also Colombia, Hong Kong and even ice hockey. It doesn’t matter who’s playing. What matters is how the game is going. An approach, not a recipe You could look at her ten slips and see a method worth copying. It isn’t one. It’s simply how she lives the game: patience, attention, one bet at a time. And nothing was settled in advance: a last-minute goal, a penalty, a defensive slip – and everything could have turned. Above all, her story shows you don’t have to chase big odds. It doesn’t show there’s a sure way to win. Betting is still a game, and chance is never far away. When luck has the final word For those who’d rather trust fate, AfroPari runs JackPot on Sport every month. Players who bet on sports during the month, pre-match or live, and reach a total of 7,287,404 NGN. FCFA are entered into the draw. At the end of the month, 30 winners are picked at random. Watch, wait, and let the pitch decide. 18+ · Play responsibly The post Ten live bets, zero accumulators: the story of a bettor from Burkina Faso appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Amotekun arrests suspect over alleged 200 house break-ins in Ondo
item.description: …Over 200 master keys recovered from suspect By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Security Network Agency, Amotekun Corps, has arrested a suspected serial housebreaker, identified as Michael Morayo, for allegedly breaking into more than 200 houses across different parts of the state. Morayo was among 13 suspected criminals paraded by the security outfit in Akure, the state capital. He was reportedly arrested in the Ijomu area of Akure. According to the Amotekun Corps, the suspect allegedly operated alone for about six years, breaking into houses and stealing household items, which he subsequently sold through an online marketplace he reportedly established. The security outfit said the suspect maintained an affluent lifestyle, dressed elegantly and spoke politely, making it difficult for people to suspect his alleged criminal activities. It added that he operated a warehouse where he kept stolen items and was meticulous in carrying out his operations. Parading the suspects, the State Commander of Amotekun, Chief Adetunji Adeleye, said Morayo allegedly confessed to breaking into more than 200 houses. Adeleye disclosed that over 200 master keys were recovered from him, explaining that the suspect often gained access to houses without forcing doors or breaking locks. “He does not always break doors to gain access to houses. We recovered well over 200 master keys from him. He also confessed that he usually finds ways of visiting people under different pretences. “In the process, he checks their doors and, while engaging them in conversation, removes one of their spare keys,” Adeleye said. He advised residents against keeping multiple keys in their door locks, warning that the practice could expose their homes to burglars. According to him, the suspect sometimes allegedly removed keys from doors and kept them in his pocket to gain access to the houses later. Adeleye further alleged that Morayo had other methods of gaining entry into homes, including making occupants fall asleep before stealing household equipment. The Amotekun commander said the suspect’s lifestyle and manner of presentation often shielded him from suspicion. He assured that all 13 suspects arrested and paraded by the corps would face prosecution after investigations. “After detailed investigations, they will be charged before courts of competent jurisdiction, depending on the offences they are suspected to have committed,” he said. item.title: Plateau will overcome insecurity, Jonathan says
item.description: …Hails Mutfwang’s unity initiative By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Former President Goodluck Ebele Jonathan has expressed optimism that Plateau State will overcome its lingering security challenges, describing the annual Plateau Unity Christmas Carols and Praise Festival as an important platform for reconciliation, peaceful coexistence and lasting peace. Jonathan, who commended Governor Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang for promoting unity through the annual religious gathering, spoke on Friday night at the third edition of the festival held at the Ten Commandments Prayer Altar, Jos. The festival, which began on November 27, 2026, brought together Christian leaders, traditional rulers, choristers, government officials and worshippers from within and outside the state to celebrate Christmas and promote unity among residents. The former president acknowledged the security challenges Plateau had experienced over the years but expressed confidence that the unity being promoted through the festival would help address divisions and strengthen relationships among communities. He commended the state government for sustaining the initiative, describing it as an important platform for bringing people together through worship and shared values. Jonathan also expressed confidence in Mutfwang’s commitment to promoting unity, while praying for divine intervention and the restoration of lasting peace in the state. He equally applauded former Governor Jonah David Jang for his contributions to leadership in Plateau State. Earlier, Mutfwang described the festival as a divine initiative established three years ago to unite the people under the banner of God, stressing that unity was essential to overcoming the challenges confronting the state. Declaring the event open, the governor expressed confidence in God’s protection, saying that despite the forces working against Plateau, the people would not be overwhelmed. He said: “If it were left to the forces that are arrayed against Plateau, we will not be gathered here tonight. But God has told us in His word that we will pass through the fires, we will not be consumed. We will pass through the waters, we will not be overwhelmed.” Mutfwang explained that the festival was conceived not merely as a musical celebration but as an opportunity for spiritual renewal, reconciliation and the removal of barriers to unity among residents. Citing Psalm 133:1, which states that “how good and pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity,” he expressed hope that the gathering would help break down walls of division, bitterness, hatred and mutual suspicion. He urged residents to renew their commitment to love, togetherness and the collective progress of the state. item.title: A Weekend For Proof
item.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.

item.title: Trump proposes new tariffs on China, EU, 12 others
item.description: By Vera Anyagafu US President Donald Trump has proposed a new round of tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China and the European Union. The proposals were announced on Wednesday, November 25, by the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) after an eight-month investigation into what Washington calls ‘structural excess capacity’. The US says the targeted countries are promoting production through subsidies and other industrial policies, allowing them to flood world markets with cheap goods and undercut American manufacturers. The 14 economies targeted are China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. Mexico and Norway were also investigated but have been spared for now. China faces a proposed rate of 20 per cent on most products, which would be added to tariffs imposed during Trump’s first term, but would not stack on top of more recent forced-labour tariffs. According to a senior US official, the rate could double to 40 per cent if talks between Washington and Beijing fall apart. Products from the EU will be taxed at 15 per cent in compliance with the US deal with the bloc, though USTR said that could also rise to as much as 20 per cent. The new tariffs are being proposed under Section 301 of the 1974 US Trade Act, which allows Washington to penalise countries it determines are treating US businesses unfairly. The proposals are still subject to a public comment process, with comments closing on January 5, 2027, and a public hearing starting January 25, 2027, before any final action. However, Beijing has rejected the accusations, with Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun saying the so-called overcapacity is a false issue, and China opposes using it as an excuse for political manipulation. item.title: Gombe APC inaugurates 35-member legal directorate
item.description: …Tahir warns against sidelining lawyers after elections By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has inaugurated a 35-member Legal Affairs Directorate of its 2027 General Elections Campaign Council, comprising four Senior Advocates of Nigeria (SANs), all indigenes of the state. The inauguration, held at Tamusa Resort, Gombe, on Friday, brought together legal practitioners tasked with protecting the party’s interests before, during and after the 2027 general elections. Speaking at the ceremony, the Director of the Legal Affairs Directorate, Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, described the inclusion of four Gombe indigenes in the Inner Bar as a significant milestone in the political and legal history of the state. Tahir commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and the APC leadership for assembling experienced legal practitioners, particularly those with expertise in electoral matters and litigation. He said the directorate would play a critical role in safeguarding the party’s interests across all electoral contests, from the presidential election to the state House of Assembly polls. Describing the legal directorate as one of the strategic centres of the campaign council, Tahir said its responsibilities would go beyond election-day activities to include pre-election legal advice, protection of party members against unlawful arrests and harassment, electoral monitoring and post-election litigation. He noted that some of the most demanding responsibilities of the legal team would begin after voting, when lawyers would be required to collate electoral evidence, obtain certified documents, prepare witnesses and develop legal arguments to defend the party’s position. According to him, while political leaders and supporters might conclude their activities after campaigns and voting, lawyers would remain engaged in preparing legal documents, researching electoral laws and responding to emerging legal challenges. Tahir said the directorate was committed to deploying its professional expertise and collective experience to protect the interests of the party and its candidates throughout the electoral process. However, he appealed to the party leadership not to sideline members of the directorate in favour of external legal practitioners when post-election disputes arise. He urged the party to ensure that lawyers who had worked at the grassroots and gathered relevant electoral intelligence were integrated into legal teams handling election petitions. “We implore the party and its leadership not to jettison, forget and abandon these committed lawyers in preference for outside legal practitioners in the event of legal challenges at the tribunal,” he said. Tahir argued that members of the directorate who had participated actively in the electoral process possessed valuable firsthand knowledge that could strengthen legal representation and the presentation of evidence. item.title: 2027: Nnaji unveils manifesto, promises free healthcare for elderly
item.description: .. PDP candidate pledges industrialisation, four-year tenure, tax relief, lower rents, school fees The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has promised free medical treatment for residents aged 70 and above if elected governor in the 2027 governorship election. Nnaji made the pledge on Friday during the unveiling of his manifesto and inauguration of the party’s campaign council in Enugu, where he also promised to industrialise the state, reduce the cost of living and improve residents’ welfare. He said his proposed administration would establish a dedicated hospital for elderly residents, where people aged 70 and above would receive medical treatment without paying hospital bills. “At the age of 70, the government under me will have a special hospital. We will set it up as soon as I’m in. Once you are 70 years, we will have a dedicated hospital. Everybody that is 70 will never pay for hospital bill in Enugu State,” he said. The PDP candidate said the programme would be funded through the state’s internally generated revenue and federal allocations, insisting that government resources must translate into tangible benefits for residents. Nnaji also promised to reduce school fees and rents, alongside a four-year tax relief programme aimed at easing the financial burden on households. “Four years of no tax. We will remove the taxes. Four years of reducing rent. The rentages will go down. People can now enjoy living in somebody’s house,” he said. Unveiling the manifesto, Nnaji described the document as a covenant with the people of Enugu State, pledging to serve only one four-year term if elected. “I am going to do just one tenure of four years. It is more than enough,” he said. He criticised the manifesto of the incumbent administration, describing what he called unfulfilled promises as a “yahoo-yahoo manifesto”. Nnaji cited previous promises on water supply, alleging that the government had failed to deliver on its commitment to provide water within 180 days despite three years having elapsed. The PDP candidate said his proposed administration would focus on recovering, rebuilding and industrialising the state, with emphasis on job creation, economic growth and tackling insecurity. He said the proposed industrialisation programme would create direct and indirect employment opportunities for thousands of young people. “The essence of industrialisation we are doing is to create jobs. Jobs for our children,” he said. On education, Nnaji promised to rehabilitate abandoned public schools rather than concentrate government resources on expensive new projects. He argued that the amount spent on constructing one smart school could be used to renovate several existing schools. “One point something billion they use in building one smart school… can repair 82 schools. item.title: 2027 Polls: INEC begins nationwide mock accreditation; 490 units in Lagos
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is conducting a six-hour nationwide mock voter accreditation exercise today, Saturday, as part of preparations for the 2027 general elections. The exercise, scheduled to run from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., is designed to assess the operational readiness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), test the real-time transmission of results to the INEC Result Viewing (IReV) portal and identify possible technical and logistical challenges ahead of the main elections. INEC clarified that the exercise is not an actual election but a test run to ensure the efficiency of its electoral technologies ahead of the presidential and National Assembly elections scheduled for January 16, 2027. Nationwide, the exercise is taking place in 17,676 polling units, comprising two selected polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas. Only registered voters whose polling units have been selected for the exercise are expected to participate. 490 polling units in Lagos In Lagos State, 490 polling units will participate in the exercise, representing two polling units in each of the 245 registration areas across the state’s 20 local government areas. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Lagos State, Prof. Ayobami Salami, said the comprehensive list of selected polling units had been displayed at all INEC local government offices to enable residents to confirm their locations. Meanwhile, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has cancelled the November monthly environmental sanitation exercise, which was originally scheduled for today, to ensure unrestricted movement and encourage residents’ participation in the mock accreditation exercise. In Lagos Central Senatorial District, approximately 148 polling units across five local government areas have been selected for the exercise. The breakdown shows that Surulere Local Government Area has 46 polling units across 23 wards, including Aguda, Ijeshatedo, Itire, Ikate, Orile and Coker. Lagos Island has 40 polling units across 20 wards, including Araromi Odo, Epetedo, Idumagbo, Lafiaji, Olosun, Eiyekole and Okepopo. Lagos Mainland has 22 polling units across 11 wards, covering areas such as Ebute Metta, Glover, Alagomeji, Oyingbo, Iwaya and Yaba. Apapa has 20 polling units across 10 wards, including Apapa I–IV and Iganmu, while Eti-Osa also has 20 polling units across 10 wards, covering Ikoyi-Obalende, Victoria Island I and II, Ikoyi I and II, Iru/Victoria Island, Ilasan, Ajah, Sangotedo and Awoyaya. INEC urged eligible voters in the selected polling units to participate in the exercise within the six-hour window to familiarise themselves with the accreditation technology and help ensure a seamless voting process during the 2027 elections. However, as of 7:30 a.m. on Saturday, no activity had been recorded at the selected polling units, as voters were yet to arrive for the exercise. item.title: Live Updates: INEC Mock Accreditation
item.description: It’s about seven weeks before the 2027 general election, and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. According to him, the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. Amupitan said the Commission had procured new accreditation machines and set a lower voter threshold for the actual election in January. “INEC will deploy over 1.41 million ad hoc personnel alongside 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, calibrated at a reduced threshold of 850 voters per machine,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. The exercise is expected to stimulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. item.title: Obi, Makinde, Dino, others embrace at Dunamis Church
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, on Friday attended an all-night service at the headquarters of Dunamis International Gospel Centre (DIGC) in Abuja, where they joined other political figures in prayers for Nigeria and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections. Also present at the service were African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain, Dino Melaye, and an aide to Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori. The service, held at the church’s Glory Dome, formed part of activities marking the 30th anniversary of Dunamis, founded in November 1996 by Pastor Paul Enenche and his wife, Becky, both medical doctors turned pastors. The anniversary celebration featured the church’s annual week-long Kingdom Power and Glory World Conference (KPGWC), with this year’s edition themed, “Opened Heaven”. The conference attracted delegates from 82 countries, including Nigeria. At about 1 a.m. on Saturday, Enenche invited Obi, Makinde and Melaye to the altar for a special prayer session for Nigeria. They were joined by Oborevwori’s aide, who represented the All Progressives Congress (APC), and another church member representing the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). During the session, Enenche asked the five representatives to hold hands as he led the congregation in prayers anchored on Job 42:10. The prayer points included a plea for God’s perfect will to prevail in Nigeria, and for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct the 2027 elections fairly. The congregation also prayed for the smooth functioning of electoral systems and equipment, including the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as reliable internet connectivity during the elections. They further prayed for credible elections without bloodshed, crisis or post-election violence. Before the prayer session, the church’s South-South Coordinator, David Majiyebo, announced the presence of Melaye, Makinde, Obi and a former government minister, drawing a loud ovation from worshippers. After the session, which lasted less than 15 minutes, Enenche reminded the politicians that earthly life was temporary and that everyone would eventually stand before God to account for how they used the power entrusted to them. He also noted that genuine churches accommodate members with different political affiliations. Enenche subsequently asked the political representatives to shake hands and embrace one another as a demonstration of unity and the absence of bitterness. The politicians exchanged handshakes and embraces without making speeches. The pastor later asked the congregation whether the joint prayer session was good for Nigeria, and the worshippers responded in the affirmative. item.title: CHINA DIARIES: Where Students Build the Future
item.description: I must confess, I was not quite prepared for what I saw during my visit to the Qinling Workshop at Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College in China. For someone fascinated by technology and innovation, walking into the institution’s aircraft hangar was an experience in itself. There were aircraft and helicopters, aviation equipment and specialised training facilities. For a moment, it felt less like visiting a school and more like stepping into an aviation engineering centre. But the biggest surprise was yet to come. Beyond the aircraft and helicopters, I encountered something that left an even stronger impression: drones designed, developed and assembled by students. China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents China Diaries: The future of farming These were not simply classroom models or academic projects put together to earn grades. The students were experimenting with different drone technologies, exploring their applications and developing solutions to practical problems. There were different designs and innovations, reflecting the creativity, technical confidence and curiosity of young people who were not waiting until graduation to start making a contribution to society. It was exciting to see. One could immediately imagine the possibilities: drones that could help farmers monitor crops and spray farmlands, support environmental monitoring, conduct aerial surveys, inspect infrastructure and assist emergency response operations. What struck me most was the philosophy behind what I was seeing. Technology was not being taught as an abstract subject. Students were being encouraged to understand problems and develop technological solutions. An institution built around practical skills The Qinling Workshop visit offered an opportunity to appreciate the work of Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College, an institution with a strong focus on aviation, engineering and technical education. Its programmes cover a wide range of disciplines, including aviation manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, aircraft engine technology, drone application technology, general aviation, mechanical engineering, artificial intelligence, computer technology, robotics, automation, electronic information, aviation logistics and automotive technology. Students also study specialised areas such as CNC machining, intelligent manufacturing, aircraft electronic systems, materials engineering, welding technology, surveying and remote sensing, software development, big data, airport operations and civil aviation services. The breadth of these programmes is significant. It shows an understanding that an aviation and manufacturing economy requires much more than pilots and aircraft engineers. It needs technicians, software developers, mechanics, materials specialists, electronics experts, maintenance professionals and people who can design, manufacture and repair equipment.
